findings.message: Avoid non-native interactive elements. The root <div> has an onKeyDown handler (roving Arrow/Home/End focus) but no interactive role.

codeReview.issue: The Arrow/Home/End handler is attached to the root static <div> (onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}). This trips jsx-a11y/no-static-element-interactions as an error, so `npm run lint` fails and the components-check CI gate cannot pass. The delegation also brings extra complexity: the target.matches('[data-accordion-header]') and closest('[data-accordion]') scoping exists only because the listener sits on the container.
codeReview.fix: Move the key handling onto each header <button>, which is a native interactive element, via its onKeyDown. Put a ref or getHeaders() on the Accordion context so the button can find its sibling headers (still scoped to the nearest [data-accordion]). Keep the consumer's onKeyDown on the root as a plain pass-through, and do not add a role to the root div to silence the rule.

codeReview.issue: .chevron is absolutely positioned against .item, not the header button. When an item is open the chevron is centred on the whole item, which matches reference.png, but it then sits over the panel area with pointer-events:none. Clicking the visible chevron-up therefore lands on the panel, not the button, so the most obvious close target does nothing. The hover overlay also covers only the header, not the area where the chevron is drawn.
codeReview.fix: Keep the visual position but make the chevron area act as the toggle. For example, make the header button span the full item height when open (the panel then sits beside the chevron column inside the item grid), or put the chevron in a column the button owns. The simplest option: let clicks on the chevron reach toggle by removing pointer-events:none and moving the chevron outside the button as an aria-hidden element with onClick={toggle} (no extra tab stop). Check against reference.png afterwards.

codeReview.issue: styles.heading and styles.title are used but not defined in Accordion.module.css, so they resolve to undefined. These are dead classNames.
codeReview.fix: Remove className={styles.heading} and className={styles.title}, or define the classes if the styling is actually needed.

codeReview.issue: The title is rendered as a raw <span> inside the header button. The typography rule in packages/components/AGENTS.md says visible string props go through <Text>/<Heading>, never a raw <span>. The span does inherit the Heading's title-small styling, so there is no visual bug, but the convention is broken.
codeReview.fix: Drop the wrapper span (the text node inherits from Heading), or render it as <Text as="span"> only if it needs its own type style. Do not add a bare span.

codeReview.issue: ADR-023 guard wording and shape: the convention calls for Object.assign(Preset, { Root, ... }) and the error message "Parent.X must be rendered inside Parent.Root". Here the preset itself is the context root, there is no Accordion.Root, and the message is 'inside Accordion'. That works for a part-only API, but it differs from the documented contract and from how sibling composites word the guard.
codeReview.fix: Either add Accordion.Root (the preset aliases it) and use the canonical message, or record in metadata composition.parts / the API proposal why this composite uses the root-as-provider form. Update the test's expected message to match.

codeReview.issue: The AccordionItemProps spread type omits 'onClick' from the item wrapper <div>, but the wrapper does not own onClick (the inner button does). The Omit is arbitrary. Meanwhile AccordionProps leaves 'role' open on the root.
codeReview.fix: Narrow the spread types to the attributes the component actually owns or forbids: Omit 'role' on the root, and drop 'onClick' from the Item Omit unless a documented antiPattern requires it.

a11y.issue: The keyboardInteractions entry 'Tab / Shift+Tab: Moves focus between section headers and any focusable content in open panels' is only partly tested. The test covers forward Tab across headers only. It does not test Shift+Tab, and it does not test that focusable content inside an open panel is in the tab sequence (or that content in a closed, hidden panel is skipped).
a11y.fix: Extend 'reaches every header with Tab': put a focusable element (e.g. a <button> or <a href>) inside an open item and inside a closed item. Assert that Tab goes header -> panel content -> next header, skips the closed panel's content, and that user.tab({ shift: true }) reverses the order.

a11y.issue: The root-level roving handler scopes headers with closest('[data-accordion]') so that nested accordions or non-header targets are ignored, but no test checks this. Arrow/Home/End pressed inside panel content (e.g. a text input or a nested Accordion) must not move focus to the outer headers. This is the riskiest branch of the keyboard logic, and it goes untested while the handler is being moved to fix the lint error.
a11y.fix: Add a test: focus an element inside an open panel, press ArrowDown/Home, and assert focus did not move and the default was not prevented. If nested accordions stay possible despite canNest:false, add a test that ArrowDown on an inner header cycles only the inner headers.

a11y.issue: Parts of the declared aria contract are not asserted: the chevron is aria-hidden, and the region's aria-labelledby equals the button id (only the region's accessible name is checked). The aria-controls/region wiring is checked for the open item only, so the closed item's panel being hidden from the accessibility tree is not checked via a role query with { hidden: true }.
a11y.fix: Assert that the chevron wrapper has aria-hidden="true" and that the panel has aria-labelledby equal to button.id. Assert that queryByRole('region', { name: /One/ }) is null while One is closed and present after it opens.

a11y.issue: The subtitle renders inside the header <button>, which is inside the heading, so the heading's and button's accessible name becomes 'The Anthropologist 4 hours, 30min'. The APG pattern allows this, but it makes heading-navigation lists verbose, and the subtitle is not tied to the title as a description.
a11y.fix: Optional: keep the title as the button's name (aria-labelledby on a title span id) and expose the subtitle via aria-describedby. Otherwise, document in metadata accessibility that the subtitle is part of the accessible name.
